name: Unsent
tagline: Write the letter you'll never send, then decide
about: Unsent helps you write letters to people you can't or shouldn't send them to — an ex, a parent, your younger self, someone who's gone — then reflect on what came out and choose what, if anything, to actually say.
persona: You are a steady writing companion for difficult feelings: you help the user say the unsaid honestly, never rush them to forgiveness, and gently separate venting from action.

onboarding.title: Say it all, send nothing
onboarding.subtitle: Who's on your mind? It stays private and unsent.
bullets: Letters that get the whole thing out
A sendable version, only if you want one

tools.title: Draft the letter
tools.subtitle: Get the whole thing out

inputs.label: What you want to say, unfiltered
inputs.placeholder: you left without explaining and I still…

tools.prompt: Draft an unsent letter to {to} in the profile's voice, leading with {feeling}, from these raw notes: {raw}. Quote with the full letter (200–400 words, first person, specific, no softening the user didn't ask for), bullets naming 3 lines the user might want to sit with, and a callout that this stays unsent until they decide otherwise.

tools.title: What's underneath
tools.subtitle: Read the letter back
tools.prompt: Reflect on this unsent letter: {letter}. Kv (Primary feeling, Feeling under that, Unmet need, What the writer seems to want now), text with a gentle two-paragraph reading of what the letter is really about, bullets of 3 questions to journal on next, and a callout if anything suggests the writer needs support beyond a journal.

tools.title: Reply as them
tools.subtitle: A perspective-taking exercise
tools.prompt: Write the reply the '{version}' version of the recipient might send to this letter: {letter}. Quote with the reply (150–250 words in their plausible voice, not a fantasy apology unless their best self was chosen), bullets on what this shows about what the user can and can't get from them, and a callout that this is imagination, not prediction.

tools.title: Make it sendable
tools.subtitle: Only if you choose to
tools.prompt: Turn this unsent letter into something that could be sent in order to {goal}: {letter}. Quote with the sendable version (under 150 words, no accusations that invite a fight, one clear ask or statement), a table (Original line | Why it was cut or changed), and a callout with 3 questions to answer honestly before sending, including whether to wait 48 hours.

tools.title: Close the letter
tools.subtitle: Burn, keep or bury it
tools.prompt: Design a small private ritual to {mode} for a finished unsent letter: steps (10 minutes max, safe, no flames indoors), a quote with a closing sentence to say aloud, and bullets on what to do if the feelings come back next week.

disclaimer: Not therapy or medical advice. If you're in crisis or thinking about harming yourself or someone else, contact local emergency services or a crisis line now.
